title: Spain Wins the Biggest World Cup Ever — But Was It Too Big?
summary:
Imagine a soccer tournament so huge that 48 countries played instead of the usual 32. That's what happened at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which just ended with Spain beating Argentina in the final. But the biggest World Cup ever left everyone asking: was it too big? And what about those annoying drink breaks?

First, the good stuff. More teams meant more surprises. Cape Verde, a tiny island nation, played in their first World Cup and became everyone's favorite underdog. They tied with Spain and Uruguay and almost beat Argentina! It showed that the gap between the best teams and the rest is getting smaller. For fans, there were more games, more stories, and new heroes to cheer for.

But not everything was perfect. The tournament was so long that it felt like a lifetime ago when it started. And those hydration breaks? Fans in the stadiums booed loudly every time the game stopped so players could drink water. They said it broke the flow of the match. FIFA said the breaks were needed because of the heat, but many people think 45-minute halves should be played without interruption.

There was also a lot of drama off the field. The U.S., one of the host countries, was in a conflict with Iran, another team in the tournament. A ceasefire (when both sides agree to stop fighting) was announced just before the World Cup began, but the fighting started again after Iran's team was knocked out. This made it hard for some fans and players to get visas to travel.

Now, some people are already talking about making the next World Cup in 2030 even bigger — with 64 teams! That would mean even more countries like Italy or Nigeria could join. But would it be too much? For now, Spain is celebrating their victory, and fans are already counting down to the next one.
why_it_matters: This story matters because it shows that even a soccer game can be changed by heat and faraway wars, making you think about what makes a tournament truly fun.

background_read: The FIFA World Cup (organized by FIFA, soccer’s global governing body) happens every four years and before 2026, it had 32 teams.
Cape Verde, a small island nation off West Africa, has a population of about half a million and had never played in a World Cup before.
A ceasefire, like the one between the U.S. and Iran, is a temporary halt in fighting, often used to allow peace talks or to protect civilians.
